title: The Promise of Port Alder
premise: Rosalind Delacroix inherits her late father's debt-ridden vineyard in Port Alder and a family reunion invitation she dreads, where her successful cousins will measure her failure. Desperate, she persuades Julian Marsh—a ferry captain and the town's reluctant golden boy—to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake romance turns real just as Rosalind discovers the vineyard's debts trace back to Julian's own family, who want the land for a marina development. Torn between saving her inheritance and protecting a love that was never supposed to be real, Rosalind must publicly claim both her vineyard and her heart before the last ferry of the season carries Julian—and her chance at belonging—away for good.
about_author: E. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade working coastal vineyards before turning to writing full-time. She lives on a small island where the ferries truly do stop running in winter.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Three years after inheriting Delacroix Vineyard, Rosalind opens another foreclosure notice and counts what's left: eleven barrels, a leaking roof, and a cellar cat named Brutus. When her mother calls about the annual family reunion, Rosalind lies that she's bringing someone. The beat: weary defiance masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Man on the Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Ferry captain Julian Marsh watches Rosalind miss the last crossing by thirty seconds and offers her a ride back from the mainland dock anyway. Their banter is easy in a way neither expects. He mentions, offhand, that he dreads his own family obligations too. The beat: unexpected kinship between two people pretending to be fine.

chapters.title: A Reckless Proposition
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Cornered by her mother's follow-up call, Rosalind tracks Julian down at the harbor café and proposes a deal: he plays her boyfriend for the reunion weekend; she'll help him charm the town council into backing his ferry expansion petition. Julian hesitates, then agrees. The beat: nervous exhilaration over a bargain that feels like a dare.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over cheap wine in the vineyard's crumbling tasting room, they draft rules: no real feelings, no ex-talk, hand-holding permitted. The scene crackles as proximity makes the rules feel absurd. Julian notices the vineyard's beauty beneath its decay; Rosalind notices him noticing. The beat: attraction disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Arriving at Alder House
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They drive to the reunion at her family's estate, rehearsing their story—how they met (the ferry), how long (four months). Her cousin Vivienne greets them with a smile sharp enough to draw blood, and Rosalind realizes Julian's presence has made her visible for the first time in years. The beat: terror and thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: The Performance Begins
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At dinner, Julian charms the Delacroix clan effortlessly, but when Rosalind's uncle mocks the vineyard's debts, Julian defends her work with quiet conviction that startles everyone—including Rosalind. Later, holding hands under the table, the performance stops feeling like acting. The beat: the fake beginning to feel dangerously true.

chapters.title: Dessert and Complications
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. By dessert, her grandmother has invited 'Julian' to stay the whole weekend, and Vivienne corners Rosalind with a knowing look: 'He looks at you like you matter.' Rosalind flees to the garden, where Julian finds her, and an almost-kiss is interrupted by fireworks. The beat: desire outrunning the script.

chapters.title: Midnight Confessions
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Unable to sleep, Julian and Rosalind talk on the estate's dock until 3 a.m.—her father's death, his brother lost at sea, why they both hide behind duty. They fall asleep on the dock cushions, hands intertwined. The beat: intimacy built on shared grief rather than pretense.

chapters.title: Sunday Morning Fallout
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Waking tangled together, they're caught by Rosalind's grandmother, who is delighted rather than scandalized. But driving home, Julian goes quiet, and Rosalind catches him studying a marina development proposal with his family's name on it—one that lists waterfront parcels including, she realizes with dread, hers. The beat: first crack in the fairy tale.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Shows
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Back home, Rosalind digs through her father's old files and discovers the vineyard's crushing loans came from Marsh Family Holdings—Julian's family bought her father's debt years ago. The man she's falling for is entangled in her ruin. The beat: betrayal arriving before confirmation.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rosalind confronts Julian at the docks. He swears he didn't know his family held her debt—he left the family business after his brother's death—but admits they've been pressuring him to come home and endorse the marina. Rosalind can't tell truth from performance anymore. The beat: trust fracturing under the weight of coincidence.

chapters.title: The Council Meeting
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At the town council, Julian presents his ferry petition, but his mother arrives unannounced and reveals the Marsh plan: the marina will make the ferry route obsolete. Julian's petition dies in real time, and he watches Rosalind leave the room without looking back. The beat: public humiliation and private heartbreak.

chapters.title: Silence on the Line
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Two weeks of silence. Rosalind throws herself into harvest prep alone, refusing help even from her loyal neighbor Mrs. Okonkwo. A letter arrives from Marsh Holdings: final notice—the vineyard will be auctioned unless she sells voluntarily within sixty days. The beat: isolation chosen as armor.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Warning
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Vivienne visits unexpectedly—not to gloat but to confess: she once loved someone her family disapproved of and chose duty, and she's regretted it for fifteen years. She urges Rosalind not to repeat her mistake. Rosalind insists this isn't love; it was never real. The beat: a mirror held up to denial.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. A storm damages the harbor and strands supply boats. Julian organizes relief runs, and when he learns the vineyard's access road is flooded, he drives supplies out despite everything. He and Rosalind argue in the rain—raw, honest, unfinished. Neither apologizes; both remember. The beat: anger revealing how deep the feeling runs.

chapters.title: The Mother's Offer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Julian's mother, Eleanor Marsh, visits the vineyard with an offer: sell now, keep a settlement, and she'll ensure Julian keeps his ferry contract. She calls Rosalind a distraction her son can't afford. Rosalind nearly signs—until she sees Julian's name already crossed off the company letterhead. He's been cut loose. The beat: temptation meeting revelation.

chapters.title: Choosing Sides
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confronts his mother and formally walks away from Marsh Holdings, surrendering his inheritance to testify against the marina at the county hearing. His father disowns him in one sentence. Standing in the empty family office, Julian feels lighter than he has in years. The beat: freedom purchased at the price of belonging.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the county hearing, Julian testifies against the marina, exposing the debt scheme that targeted struggling farms including Delacroix Vineyard. The project stalls pending investigation. Rosalind watches him sacrifice everything and understands she's been guarding a heart she already gave away. The beat: awe dissolving the last resistance.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Despite the hearing, the auction proceeds in ten days. Rosalind inventories the vineyard one last time and finds her father's hidden ledger: proof the original loan terms were predatory, enough to void the sale—if she can get it authenticated before the auction. She needs Julian's knowledge of maritime law from his former life. The beat: hope requiring the risk of asking.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The day before the auction is also the last ferry run of the season. Rosalind boards with the ledger and finds Julian at the helm. Amid passengers and salt wind, she asks for his help—and tells him she loves him, no conditions, no performance. He says it back before she finishes. The beat: the whole heart, finally risked.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With Julian's testimony and the authenticated ledger, the auction is halted and the predatory loans voided; the vineyard is Rosalind's, debt-free but humble. Eleanor Marsh, facing exposure, retreats. Rosalind plants new vines with Julian beside her, and her grandmother declares him family before the first row is finished. The beat: hard-won victory and rootedness.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Months later, the ferry resumes spring service with Julian as captain and Rosalind's wine—labeled 'Promise'—in the onboard café. They've stopped keeping rules; there are none left to break. On the dock at dusk, Julian asks what she'd have done if he'd taken the last ferry and never come back. She answers: waited for the next season. The beat: belonging earned, love chosen daily.
